text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police detain three thieves after an exchange of gunfire on Saturday near the house of Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri. Security sources in the Interior Ministry deny the incident was an attempt to assassinate the prime minister.
- 536 prisoners released on the occasion of Eid al-Fitr.
- Unified companies law to be discussed after the Eid. It removes all barriers to foreign ownership and allows them to open representative and technical offices in Egypt.
- Egypt affirms it will continue to take an active role in the peace process and the need to stick to agreements.
- Companies law to encourage investment and retain the participation of workers in profits. It will also streamline steps for setting up companies.
- 470 million pounds worth of trade on the Cairo bourse last week.
- Egypt is the fifth best country for investment, according to a final report published at the Davos economic forum.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Saudi Arabia's defence minister speak by telephone to exchange Eid greetings.
